messages:
rhea: quick heads-up — ran a focused stability sweep for muon11b hybrid-int6 on canary yesterday. saw two patterns: (1) small gen-quality regressions on code-heavy long-contexts, (2) intermittent slab churn causing slow allocs and 503s under sustained batches. summary below.

jordan: high level numbers?

rhea: paste snapshot: ```
variant        | p50 | p95 | long-qa-em F1 | regen-rate | observed OOMs
int4 (prod)    | 114 | 335 | 0.813         | 0.9%       | 0/6h
hybrid-int6    | 98  | 305 | 0.802         | 1.8%       | 3/6h (spikes)
int6-stable    | 105 | 320 | 0.810         | 1.1%       | 0/6h
```

rhea: note: long-qa-em is our long-form conv QA eval (1k+ context). regen-rate = percent of responses requiring >1 regen to satisfy prompt heuristics.

mira: thanks. int6-stable refers to hybrid variant with per-token calibration and stochastic-rounding on kv, right?

rhea: yes — we tried two mitigations: per-token scale-correction for attention accumulators and enabling stochastic rounding during kv quant writes. that brought F1 up from 0.802 -> 0.810 but increased latency a bit.
kai: latency delta?

rhea: p50 from 98 -> 105ms, p95 ~+15ms. acceptable for short requests but still worth gating for long-context routes.
jordan: where do OOMs come from? pattern?

rhea: OOMs line up with sustained high-batch bursts (>10 sustained) and generation windows >512. stack shows repeated slab growth attempts then compactor thrash. dev logs: "alloc_by_stripe: retry 2->4, slab_grow: success then slow reclaim".
mira: can we pre-warm kv cache allocations per instance during startup to reduce slab growth events?
kai: yes — we experimented with a lightweight warmup: touch-kv prefixes up to 128 stripes; reduces first-hour churn but increases base memory by ~8MB. tradeoff small for stability.
jordan: suggestion: create two canary flavors: hybrid-int6-warm (pre-warm + stochastic rounding + per-token scale) and hybrid-int6-light (only per-token scale). then route short prompts to warm and long prompts to int4 fallback.
rhea: good plan. also propose a dynamic batch cap: if prompt_len > 1024 then cap batch_size at 6; else allow 12. we saw fewer OOMs with that rule.
mira: what about eval gating? need a formal gate for rollout.
kai: gating rules proposal: 1) perf-bot runs perf matrix (latency+mem) and QA eval (500 long-convo prompts) every 30m during canary; 2) if long-qa-em delta >1% or regen-rate >1.5% then fail canary; 3) if OOM rate >0.3% over 30m then immediate rollback.
jordan: add monitoring for slab_churn and kv_writes_failed metric too. set alert thresholds: slab_churn > 10% 10m, kv_writes_failed > 5m spikes.
rhea: I'll add those to the dashboard. also adding a small telemetry change: capture tokenization boundary cases where byte-level tokenization causes extra tokens for code fences — that matched many bad examples.
mira: nice catch. If tokenization is inflating context length, dynamic cap formula should use normalized_length = floor(token_count/1.05) for muon since it tokenizes dense.
kai: ops-wise, implement runtime flags: kv_prewarm=true/false, kv_stoch_rounding=true/false, per_token_scale=1.0 (float). default all false; canary will flip for warm variant. config snippet: {"kv_prewarm_stripes":128, "kv_stoch_rounding":true, "per_token_scale":0.996} (commit will have exact keys).
jordan: who owns the PR?
rhea: I will. plan: branch muon/hybrid-canary-stability, include unit tests for kv_stoch_rounding determinism and a replay harness to compare F1 across seeds.
mira: timeline?
rhea: PR by EOD, perf-bot matrix scheduled for next canary window (2am PST), will run 6h canary then expand if pass.

eng-ml-bot: perf-bot job queued id=muon-stability-8012345678-01 ETA 2h

mira: add rollback circuit: if perf-bot fails twice in a row, traffic auto routes to int4 and alert oncall with runbook link.
kai: also include a lightweight calibration step during model load: run 50 synthetic prompt combinations to calibrate per_token_scale, store in model metadata so warm instances use tuned scale.
jordan: sounds solid. please ensure evaluation harness covers both code-heavy and instruction-heavy subsets; we've seen different patterns.
rhea: will do. posting draft PR link once ready. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
